title: Chapter 244: Things You Shouldn't See
html:
The red number on the display burned against the darkness. When 24 appeared, the elevator doors opened. Fresh bloodstains slicked the corridor, and new scratches scarred the walls. The air reeked of blood, as though something terrible had just occurred. Chen Ge removed the cleaver from his calf and concealed it inside his sleeve.

“Let’s go in.”

Chen Ge did not look back; the chill behind him confirmed that Zhang Ya was following. The corridor was so quiet that every sound carried. After he had covered a third of its length, he heard sawing. Several more steps confirmed that it came from the room the bird-masked man had left during Chen Ge’s first visit.

The ten seats probably represent the original ten patients, while the bird-masked man handles menial tasks. But what is his actual role in the Ghost Stories Society?

After a moment’s thought, Chen Ge shook his head. The answer did not matter. He had not come to understand the society; he had come to destroy it. They’re all products of three-star scenarios. Zhang Ya should be able to handle them.

From outside the room, Chen Ge peered through the doorway and frowned. The bird-masked man crouched in a corner with several tools. An old man lay before him, with a mask discarded nearby. Chen Ge recognized it as the one worn earlier by newcomer No. 1.

“What are you doing?” Chen Ge blocked the door and suddenly spoke. The birdman jumped at the sudden intruder. The man did not turn around and spoke while facing away from Chen Ge. “Everyone has left; why are you still here?”

“Weren’t you serving dinner? I left for only a moment, and you’ve already finished?” Chen Ge felt a trace of regret. Whatever the reason, his plan for the night would have to change.

“A small problem arose. One member received a message from the chairperson, so they all had to leave.” The bird-masked man still did not turn. His upper body appeared frozen, his back kept toward Chen Ge and his face toward the old man on the floor.

“A message from the chairperson?” Chen Ge thought that the man was acting funny. He walked into the room. “Can you tell me where they have gone?”

“No idea.” The man paused before adding, “I suggest you stay away.”

“The elevator is the only visible exit, and I never left it. Is there another way out?” The man’s answers had already yielded several clues. With the other members gone, the bird-masked man was Chen Ge’s sole source of information.

“Someone will explain that in the future. For now, please leave.” The bird-masked man’s movements remained rigid, as though he were deliberately hiding his face. Chen Ge had not come to negotiate. Instead of leaving, he advanced farther into the room.

“Why didn’t you follow them and leave then? Do you stay here?” Chen Ge kept his questions coming.

“I’m only responsible for cleaning and cooking.”

“Interesting.” Chen Ge had begun to suspect the bird-masked man. He could remain on the twenty-fourth floor indefinitely and access every room. Could he be the chairperson? Perhaps the chairperson was not one of the ten members at all.

Chen Ge wanted proof, but a direct question would never receive an honest answer. He therefore chose the most straightforward method. Whether or not this man was the chairperson, if he disappeared forever, he could no longer fill the role.

Realizing that Chen Ge was approaching, the bird-masked man raised his voice. “Newcomer, whatever you may have done outside, here you will obey the Ghost Stories Society’s rules.”

“The rules? But there’s only one, isn’t there? I just have to tell ghost stories. What other rules are there?” Now that Chen Ge found the man suspicious, he had no intention of leaving so easily.

“Seeing what you shouldn’t carries a price. Now that the members have gone, you and I are alone on this floor.” The bird-masked man rose, accompanied by the patter of dripping liquid. Chen Ge looked down. Blood had soaked the man’s trousers and was running along his legs.

“I don’t understand your meaning. If all the members have left, that sounds like bad news for you.” Chen Ge continued forward, pretending not to notice the blood.

“Is that so?” The birdman moved to the side to reveal the old man’s body. His face was carved in terror.

“Newcomers occasionally vanish without explanation. Everyone has grown accustomed to it.” He spoke as if to himself, though clearly intending Chen Ge to hear. Then the bird-masked man turned. Neither the strange tools in his hands nor his blood-soaked clothes commanded attention like his face.

He did not need a mask!

His mouth projected from his face like a beak, and the blood vessels characteristic of monsters from behind the door writhed across his cheeks. He was not human.

“I gave you a chance, but you refused to appreciate it.” The birdlike man rattled the tools in his hands, producing an unpleasant sound. “I’ve wanted to do this since the moment we met. There were too many witnesses then, but now you’ve returned alone.”

The situation differed from Chen Ge’s expectations; he had believed he was speaking to a human.

If I’d known, I wouldn’t have wasted so much time.

Chen Ge studied the man’s face. To survive outside the door, monsters from the other side had to attach themselves to living people. The creature growing from this man’s head was a variety he had never encountered.

Their relationship probably resembled that between Xiong Qing and the thin monster. The creature grew upon its host, while the living person retained a degree of control by satisfying its desires.

All the real members of the Ghost Stories Society will have monsters attached to them. This is rather difficult, especially if they have a Red Specter among them.

Chen Ge remained still, considering the implications. Believing him terrified, the birdlike man smiled cruelly. Watching people struggle was one of the few pleasures he allowed himself, and the bloody scratches around the elevator testified to that habit.

He delighted in dragging victims into despair at the very moment they believed salvation was near.

“The Ghost Stories Society is not a charity. If you wish to have salvation, you need to pay the price!”

The birdlike man charged Chen Ge, tools raised and beak-shaped mouth shrieking.

Black hair suddenly cinched around his throat and lifted him from the floor. His legs kicked desperately, his face turning purple as the blood vessels across it scattered.

“What is this?!”
